en: Catalog number: M00545 Uniform title: Durgānityārcanakrama

Manuscript: NGMCP manuscript 5-6785, Reel No.: B 368/28 Description: Ritual Manual Notes: Manuscript selected by Dr. Mark S.G. Dyczkowski and data-entered by the staff of Muktabodha under the supervision of Dr. Anirban Dash. Revision 0: September 25, 2021.

"I offer libations to Goddess Durgā. Having thus offered the libations three times, and having offered them once with "I offer libations to the attendants of Śrī Durgā," one should bow to one's chosen deity (iṣṭadevatā) and to the Sun. Then, having emerged from the water and put on clean clothes, [one should prepare] the seat with: "Hrīṃ, obeisance to the Lotus-Seated One, the Power of the Foundation (Ādhāraśakti). Thus [is] the seat.
Having worshipped [her]:
"O Earth, by you the worlds are supported; O Goddess, you are supported by Viṣṇu."
And you, O Goddess, support me; make the seat pure. || 1 ||
Having thus offered praise and sat upon the seat, one should perform the application of the *vibhūti*. It is as follows: *Hauṃ*, salutation to Sadyojāta Śiva on the head.

Having applied the sacred ash with the following mantras: "Hauṃ, obeisance to Vāmadeva, to Śiva" on the forehead; "Hauṃ, obeisance to Aghora, to Śiva" on the chest; "Hauṃ, obeisance to Tatpuruṣa, to Śiva" on the right arm; and "Hauṃ, obeisance to Īśāna, to Śiva" on the left arm. [Thus, having applied the ash, one places it] on the left.

Salutations to the venerable gurus. Salutations to the supreme gurus. Salutations to the higher and lower gurus—on the right. Gaṃ, salutations to Gaṇeśa—on the head. Salutations to the deity Śrī Durgā—thus on the nose. Phaṭ.

Having purified both hands with the mantra, along with scents and flowers, and having performed three successive upward *tāla* gestures, one should effect the binding of the ten directions with *choṭikā* snaps. Then, visualizing a rampart of fire by means of a stream of water with the mantra "Raṃ," one should perform the purification of the elements (*bhūtaśuddhi*). It is as follows: place the two hands palms-upward on the lap.

Having performed [this], by means of the mantra *haṃ saḥ*, one [visualizes] the individual soul (*jīvātman*) in the form of a lamp-flame, together with the Kuṇḍalinī situated at the Mūlādhāra, through the path of the Suṣumṇā from the Mūlādhāra... [p. 6a] ...the Mūlādhāra.
Having pierced the six cakras known as Svādhiṣṭhāna, Maṇipūraka, Anāhata, Viśuddha, and Ājñā,
and having united [the breath] with the Supreme Self (parātman) situated within the pericarp of the thousand-petaled lotus at the head which faces downward;
one should [visualize] in one's own body from the feet up to the knees a yellow-colored square marked with a vajra, [emanating from] the syllable Laṃ.
One should meditate on the seed-syllable *vaṃ*,
the water mandala, which is white, shaped like a half-moon, extending from the knees to the navel, marked with two lotuses.

One should meditate as follows: from the navel to the heart, one should meditate on the fire-maṇḍala, which is triangular, marked with a svastika, red in color, and contains the seed-syllable *raṃ*. From the heart to the space between the eyebrows, one should meditate on the wind-maṇḍala, which is circular, smoke-colored, marked with six dots, and contains the seed-syllable *yaṃ*.

One should meditate on the seed-syllable *haṃ*, blue in color, as the mandala of space (*gaganamaṇḍala*), circular in shape, extending from the center of the eyebrows to the aperture of Brahmā (*brahmarandhra*). Then, [one should meditate on] earth, water, and fire...
p. 7a)

Having contemplated that the twenty-four principles— namely wind, space, smell, taste, form, touch, sound, nose, tongue, eye, skin, ear, speech, hands, feet, anus, genitals, primordial nature (*prakṛti*), mind (*manas*), intellect (*buddhi*), and ego (*ahaṃkāra*)—
have dissolved back into their respective causes in reverse order, one should [visualize] the syllable *yaṃ*, smoke-colored.
Having visualized the seed-syllable of air (*vāyubīja*) in the left nostril, one should fill the body by reciting it sixteen times; then,
holding the nostrils, one should perform *kuṃbhaka* (retention of breath) by reciting it sixty-four times.

Having dried up the body together with the black-colored person of sin (pāpapuruṣa) residing in the left side of the abdomen by reciting [the mantra] thirty-two times, one should exhale the breath through the right nostril. Having meditated upon the red-colored seed-syllable of fire, *raṃ*, in the right nostril, one should fill the body by reciting it sixteen times.

Holding the two nostrils, one should perform *kuṃbhaka* (retention of breath) by reciting [the mantra] sixty-four times. Having burned the body along with its sins, one should exhale the air through the left nostril as ash by reciting it thirty-two times. The syllable *yaṃ*, the seed-syllable of the Moon, is white in color; [it is located] at the left nostril.

Having held [the breath] and recited [the mantra] sixteen times, one should bring the moon to the forehead; then, by reciting the seed-syllable *vaṃ* of Varuṇa sixty-four times, [one should imagine] the nectar flowing from that lunar disc on the forehead, which consists of the letters of the Mātṛkā and is agitated [by the syllable].
Fashion the entire body; by reciting the seed-syllable *laṃ* of earth thirty-two times, the body becomes very firm.

Having visualized this, one should exhale the breath through the right nostril. Then, while recollecting the seed-syllable of space, *haṃ*, one should visualize all the limbs as being restored. Thereafter, with the mantra *so'haṃ*, one should visualize the individual soul (*jīvātman*) together with Kuṇḍalinī and the twenty-four principles (*tattvas*), each established in its own respective place.

One should perform the consecration of the vital breath (*prāṇapratiṣṭhā*). It is as follows: for this *Śrīprāṇapratiṣṭhā* mantra, Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Maheśvara are the seers (*ṛṣi*), and the Ṛg, Yajur, and Sāma Vedas are the meters (*chandas*).

The meters are the *prāṇa-śakti*, the deity is [the Self], *Āṃ* is the seed-syllable (*bīja*), *Hrīṃ* is the power (*śakti*), *Kroṃ* is the peg (*kīla*), and the application (*viniyoga*) is for the installation of the vital breaths (*prāṇasthāpana*). Salutation to the sages Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Maheśvara on the head;
salutation to the meters Ṛg, Yajus, and Sāman on the mouth; salutation to the deity Prāṇa-śakti on the heart.
Salutation to Guhya at the secret place; salutation to the seed-syllable *Āṃ* at the feet; salutation to the power (*śakti*) *Hrīṃ* on all limbs;
salutation to the *kīlaka* *Kroṃ*; [salutation] to the self consisting of ether, air, fire, water, and earth: *Aṃ Kaṃ Khaṃ Gaṃ Ghaṃ Ṅaṃ Āṃ*.
To the two thumbs, *namaḥ*. To the two index fingers, who are the essence of sound, touch, form, taste, and smell— *iṃ caṃ chaṃ jaṃ jhaṃ ṅaṃ īṃ*, *svāhā*.
Uṃ ṭaṃ ṭhaṃ ḍaṃ ḍhaṃ ṇaṃ Ūṃ! To the self of the ear, skin, eye, tongue, and nose, [I offer] with the two middle fingers, Vaṣaṭ! Eṃ taṃ thaṃ daṃ dhaṃ naṃ Aiṃ!
To the self of speech, hands, feet, anus, and genitals, [I offer] with the two ring fingers, Huṃ! Oṃ paṃ phaṃ baṃ...
Bhaṃ maṃ auṃ, to the self consisting of speech, taking, going, excretion, and pleasure, *vauṣaṭ* with the two little fingers! Aṃ yaṃ raṃ laṃ vaṃ śaṃ ṣaṃ saṃ haṃ laṃ. (p.

*Kṣaṃ aṃḥ*—to the self of mind (*manas*), intellect (*buddhi*), ego (*ahaṃkāra*), thought (*citta*), and consciousness (*vijñāna*), *phaṭ* with both palms and backs of the hands. *Aṃ kaṃ khaṃ gaṃ ghaṃ ṅaṃ āṃ*—to the self of space, wind, fire, water, and earth, *namaḥ* to the heart. *Iṃ caṃ chaṃ jaṃ jhaṃ ñaṃ*...
*Īṃ*, to the self of sound, touch, form, taste, and smell, *svāhā* to the head (*śiras*).
*Uṃ ṭaṃ ṭhaṃ ḍaṃ ḍhaṃ ṇaṃ ūṃ*, to the self of the ear, skin, eye, tongue, and nose, *vaṣaṭ* to the crest-lock (*śikhā*). *Eṃ taṃ thaṃ daṃ dhaṃ naṃ aiṃ*.
To the armor for the self consisting of speech, hands, feet, anus, and genitals: *huṃ*. Oṃ paṃ phaṃ baṃ bhaṃ maṃ auṃ.

*Vauṣaṭ* to the three eyes, whose nature consists of speech, grasping, emission, and bliss. *Oṃ yaṃ raṃ laṃ vaṃ śaṃ ṣaṃ saṃ haṃ kṣaṃ aṃ*, *phaṭ* to the weapon (*astra*), whose nature consists of mind, intellect, ego, and thought. Having performed the ritual placement (*nyāsa*) in this manner, [recite] "Seated upon a lion. Placing the hand upon the heart, [recite] *āṃ hrīṃ kroṃ yaṃ raṃ laṃ*.
VAṂ ŚAṂ ṢAṂ SAṂ HOṂ OṂ KṢAṂ SAṂ HAṂ SAḤ HRĪṂ OṂ HAṂ SAḤ— may my life-force (jīva) remain here.
ĀṂ HRĪṂ KROṂ YAṂ RAṂ LAṂ VAṂ ŚAṂ ṢAṂ SAṂ HOṂ AṂ SAṂ HAṂ SAḤ OṂ HAṂ SAḤ— [may it remain] with me.
p. 11a) All the sense faculties— ĀṂ HRĪṂ KROṂ YAṂ RAṂ LAṂ VAṂ ŚAṂ ṢAṂ SAṂ HOṂ AṂ KṢAṂ SAṂ HAṂ SAḤ HRĪṂ OṂ HAṂ SAḤ— having arrived, [enter] my speech, mind, eyes, ears, nose, and vital breaths.
"May they remain happily for a long time, svāhā! Oṃ kṣaṃ saṃ haṃ saḥ hrīṃ oṃ.
Having thus performed the *prāṇapratiṣṭhā*, one should perform the internal *mātṛkā* placement (*nyāsa*). It is as follows: of this Śrī...

For the Inner Mātṛkā-vidyā: Brahmā is the seer (ṛṣi), Gāyatrī is the meter (chandas), the Inner Mātṛkā is the deity (devatā), the consonants are the seeds (bījas), the vowels are the powers (śaktis), and its application (viniyoga) is in the Mātṛkā-nyāsa. [One should perform the assignment: "Salutation to Brahmā, the seer, on the head; salutation to Gāyatrī, the meter, in the mouth; salutation to Mātṛkā, the deity, in the heart; [salutation] in the private parts..."
Homage to the half-seeds (*bīja*). Homage to the vowels (*svara*) and powers (*śakti*) on the two feet. Homage to the Unmanifest (*avyakta*) as the pin (*kīlaka*) on all limbs. Aṃ Kaṃ Khaṃ Gaṃ.

Ghaṃ ṅaṃ āṃ, salutation to the two thumbs (aṅguṣṭhābhyāṃ namaḥ). Iṃ caṃ chaṃ jaṃ jhaṃ ñaṃ īṃ, svāhā to the two index fingers (tarjanībhyāṃ svāhā). Uṃ ṭaṃ ṭhaṃ ḍaṃ ḍhaṃ ṇaṃ Ūṃ, vaṣaṭ to the two middle fingers (madhyamābhyāṃ vaṣaṭ). Eṃ taṃ thaṃ daṃ dhaṃ naṃ AIṃ, hūṃ to the two ring fingers (anāmikābhyāṃ hūṃ). Oṃ paṃ phaṃ...

BAṂ BHAṂ MAṂ AUṂ—to the two little fingers, VAUṢAṬ. AṂ YAṂ RAṂ LAṂ VAṂ ŚAṂ ṢAṂ SAṂ HAṂ LAṂ KṢAṂ AṂḤ—to the palms and backs of the hands, PHAṬ. AṂ KAṂ KHAṂ GAṂ GHAṂ ṄAṂ ĀṂ—obeisance to the heart (HṚDAYĀYA NAMAḤ). IṂ CAṂ CHAṂ JAṂ JHAṂ ÑAṂ ĪṂ.
To the head, svāhā!
*uṃ* *ṭaṃ* *ṭhaṃ* *ḍaṃ* *ḍhaṃ* *ṇaṃ* *ūṃ*, to the crest-lock, vaṣaṭ! *eṃ* *taṃ* *thaṃ* *daṃ* *dhaṃ*...
Naṃ Aiṃ Kavacāya Huṃ | Oṃ Paṃ Phaṃ Baṃ Bhaṃ Maṃ Auṃ Netratrayāya Vauṣaṭ | Aṃ Yaṃ Raṃ Laṃ Vaṃ Śaṃ Ṣaṃ Saṃ Haṃ Laṃ Kṣaṃ Aṃḥ Astrāya Phaṭ ||
Meditative concentration.
Her face, arms, and the middle of her chest were adorned with the fifty letters of the alphabet; she wore a radiant crown bound with a crescent moon, and her full, lofty breasts were prominent.
I take refuge in the Goddess of Speech, who possesses three eyes and radiant white luster, holding in her lotus-like hands a mudrā, a rosary, a jar brimming with nectar, and a sacred mantra. || 1 ||

Having meditated thus, one should mentally place [the vowels] in clockwise order upon the sixteen-petaled lotus of the Viśuddha-cakra at the region of the throat: aṃ āṃ iṃ īṃ uṃ ūṃ ṛṃ ṝṃ ḷṃ ḹṃ eṃ aiṃ oṃ auṃ aṃ aḥ. [Then] in the heart.

In the *anāhatacakra*, the twelve-petaled lotus at the heart, one should place: *kaṃ khaṃ gaṃ ghaṃ ṅaṃ caṃ chaṃ jaṃ jhaṃ ñaṃ ṭaṃ ṭhaṃ*. At the navel, in the *maṇipūracakra*, the ten-petaled lotus, one should place: *ḍaṃ ḍhaṃ ṇaṃ taṃ thaṃ daṃ dhaṃ naṃ paṃ phaṃ*. At the region of the *liṅga*.
In the *svādhiṣṭhāna* wheel,
the six-petaled lotus, one should place the syllables *baṃ bhaṃ maṃ yaṃ raṃ laṃ* at the anus.
One should place *vaṃ*, *śaṃ*, *ṣaṃ*, and *saṃ* upon the four-petalled lotus of the *mūlādhāra-cakra*.

One should place *haṃ* and *kṣaṃ* upon the two-petalled lotus of the *ājñā-cakra* between the eyebrows. Having thus performed the internal *mātṛkā-nyāsa*, one should perform the *sṛṣṭi-mātṛkā-nyāsa*. It is as follows:

Of this mantra of the venerable Mātṛkā-Sarasvatī, Brahmā is the seer (ṛṣi), Gāyatrī is the meter (chandas), Mātṛkā-Sarasvatī is the deity (devatā), the consonants are the seed-syllables (bījas), and the vowels are the powers (śaktis). (p. 14a)

The application (*viniyoga*) is for the *sṛṣṭimātṛkā-nyāsa*. Having performed the placement (*nyāsa*) and meditation (*dhyāna*) here as well according to the *antarmātṛkā*, one should perform the placement as follows: *aṃ* namaḥ on the head; *āṃ* namaḥ on the mouth; *iṃ* namaḥ on the right eye; *īṃ* namaḥ on the left eye;
*uṃ* namaḥ on the right ear; *ūṃ* namaḥ on the left ear; *ṛṃ* namaḥ... [on the right nostril].
Ṛṃ, obeisance to the right nostril; Ṝṃ, obeisance to the left nostril; Ḷṃ, obeisance to the right cheek;
Ḹṃ, obeisance to the left cheek; Eṃ, obeisance to the upper lip; Aiṃ, obeisance to the lower lip; Oṃ, obeisance to the upper row of teeth.
Oṃ namaḥ to the row of lower teeth. Aṃ namaḥ to the head. Aṃḥ namaḥ to the mouth. Kaṃ namaḥ to the base of the right arm. Khaṃ namaḥ to the elbow. Gaṃ namaḥ to the wrist. Ghaṃ namaḥ...

Aṃ at the base of the fingers; Ṅaṃ homage to the tips of the fingers; Caṃ homage to the base of the left arm; Chaṃ homage to the elbow; Jaṃ homage to the wrist; Jhaṃ homage to the base of the fingers; Ñaṃ homage to the tips of the fingers; Ṭaṃ homage to the base of the right leg; Ṭhaṃ homage to the knee; Ḍaṃ homage...
Ḍhaṃ, obeisance to the base of the toes; ṇaṃ, obeisance to the tips of the toes. (p.
15a) Taṃ, obeisance to the base of the left foot; thaṃ, obeisance to the knee; daṃ, obeisance to the ankle; dhaṃ, obeisance...

Aṃ at the base of the fingers; Naṃ homage to the tips of the fingers; Paṃ homage to the right side of the abdomen; Phaṃ homage to the left side of the abdomen; Baṃ homage to the back; Bhaṃ homage to the navel; Maṃ homage to the belly; Yaṃ homage to the heart; Raṃ homage to the right shoulder; Laṃ homage to the crown of the head; Vaṃ homage to the left shoulder.
*Śaṃ* namaḥ from the heart to the right arm; *ṣaṃ* namaḥ from the heart to the left arm; *saṃ* namaḥ from the heart to the right foot; *haṃ* namaḥ from the heart to the left foot; *laṃ*. (p. 15b)

"Namo" at the heart and so forth, and "udare"; "kṣaṃ namo" at the heart and so forth, and "mukhe. Having thus performed the Sṛṣṭimātṛkā-nyāsa, and having performed the nyāsa of the seer (ṛṣi) and other elements as prescribed for one's own root mantra, along with the recitation (japa) and so forth, one should perform the worship. It is as follows:
*Duṃ*, obeisance to the principle of the Self (*ātmatattva*). *Duṃ*, obeisance to the principle of Knowledge (*vidyātattva*). *Duṃ*, obeisance to the principle of Śiva (*śivatattva*).
Having thus performed the ritual sipping of water (*ācamana*), and having lit the lamp:
"Obeisance to Ananta, who possesses a thousand forms, and whose feet, eyes, heads, thighs, and arms are a thousandfold."
Salutation to the eternal Puruṣa of a thousand names, who sustains thousands of millions of yugas. || 2 ||
Having thus worshipped the lamp and established the water-pot (kalaśa), one should invoke Gaṇeśa at the shoulder-region with "Gaṃ,
obeisance to Gaṇeśa," and having worshipped him, [one should invoke] Varuṇa at the mouth of the pot with "Vaṃ, obeisance to Varuṇa."

Having thus invoked, one should worship. In that very place, having invoked the nine planets beginning with the Sun, and the sixteen Mothers beginning with Gaurī, one should worship them. Having inscribed the month, fortnight, and so forth, saying "Tatsat," [one should state]: "I, who am of such-and-such name and lineage, and of such-and-such name and *varman*, for the sake of attaining all desired objects through the propitiation of my chosen deity..."
"I shall perform the worship of the deity Śrī Durgā with the assembled offerings," thus he makes the formal resolve (saṃkalpa).
Having performed the placement of the *argha* vessel, one should proceed as follows: slightly to the left of one's own front,
having drawn a mandala consisting of a triangle, a hexagon, a circle, and a square using sandalwood paste and other substances,
and having worshipped it with flowers and unbroken rice grains, saying "Obeisance to Ādhāraśakti," one should [place] the tripod (*tripadikā*) with the root mantra.

Having washed [the vessel] and installed the three-legged stand with the mantra: *Oṃ, salutation to the seat for the arghya-vessel of Śrī Durgā, whose self consists of the ten kalās of the fire-mandala*, one [offers] there to the ten kalās of Agni, beginning with Dhūmra.

*Namaḥ*. Having thus worshipped, wash the *argha* vessel with *phaṭ*. Place the *argha* vessel upon its base with: "Obeisance to the *argha* vessel of Śrī Durgā, which consists of the twelve digits (*kalā*) of the solar orb. Then, having worshipped therein with: "Obeisance to the twelve digits beginning with Tapinī," [recite] *kṣaṃ laṃ haṃ*.
saṃ ṣaṃ śaṃ vaṃ laṃ raṃ yaṃ maṃ bhaṃ baṃ phaṃ paṃ naṃ dhaṃ daṃ thaṃ taṃ ṇaṃ ḍhaṃ ḍaṃ ṭhaṃ ṭaṃ ñaṃ jhaṃ jaṃ chaṃ caṃ ṅaṃ ghaṃ gaṃ khaṃ kaṃ aṃḥ aṃ auṃ oṃ aiṃ eṃ ḹṃ ḷṃ ṝṃ ṛṃ ūṃ uṃ īṃ iṃ
Uttering "Āṃ Aṃ" in reverse order, fill the argha vessel with pure water, reciting:
"Uṃ, obeisance to the moon-maṇḍala consisting of sixteen digits, the nectar of the venerable Durgā’s argha vessel. Thus.
It should be worshipped. Having worshipped right there in the water with the mantra: "Obeisance to the sixteen digits beginning with Amṛtā," [one recites]:
"O Gaṅgā, O Yamunā, O Godāvarī, O Sarasvatī..."
O Narmadā, Sindhu, and Kāverī, establish your presence in these waters! || 1 ||
Having pierced the solar disc with the *aṅkuśa* mudrā and the mantra *krom*, [one should think:
"O Sun, the holy waters within the belly of the cosmic egg have been touched by your rays."
By that truth, O God, grant me a sacred ford at Vākara.

Having invoked the sacred waters (*tīrtha*) with this mantra, and having meditated upon the deity within that water, one should worship [the deity] three times with flowers, unbroken rice grains (*akṣata*), and so forth, using the root mantra. Then, touching the water with the right hand while reciting the root mantra—
Having consecrated it three times with the mantra, covered it with the *matsyamudrā*, rendered it nectar-like (*amṛtīkṛta*) with the syllable *vaṃ* and the *dhenumudrā*,
and having displayed the *yonimudrā* and the *śaṅkhamudrā*, [one should offer] water there [with the verse]:
"Whether impure or pure, or even in whatever state one may be..."
Whoever should remember the lotus-eyed one both externally and internally, [is liberated].
Thus, having prepared the requisites for worship, one should sprinkle oneself as well.

Then, having recollected the place, time, month, lunar date, day of the week, and so forth, preceded by *oṃ tatsat*, [one says]: "I, of such-and-such lineage and such-and-such name, through the means of pleasing my chosen deity..."

Having made the formal resolve (*saṃkalpa*): "For the sake of accomplishing all desired goals, I shall perform the worship of the deity Śrī Durgā with the materials as they have been assembled," one should draw an eight-petaled lotus with a pericarp using sandalwood paste and other substances, and outside of that, a square enclosure (*bhūpura*). Therein—
With sandalwood, unbroken rice, flowers, and so forth, [one worships] at the filaments: *Āṃ* homage to Prabhā; *Īṃ* homage to Māyā; *Ūṃ* homage to Jayā.
Eṃ, salutation to Sūkṣmā; Aiṃ, salutation to Viśuddhā; Oṃ Naṃ, salutation to Nandinī;

Auṃ, salutation to Suprabhā; Aṃ, salutation to Vijayā; Aṃḥ, salutation to Sarvasiddhidā—thus everywhere. In the center: Oṃ, salutation to the Great Lion whose weapons are diamond-claws and fangs, Huṃ Phaṭ! Thus.

One should worship. Then, having invoked the deity as described in the meditation and performed the previously mentioned *prāṇapratiṣṭhā* (consecration of the vital breath), one should say: "O Goddess of gods, who are easily accessible through devotion and accompanied by your retinue, remain firmly established here for as long as I shall worship you."

Having thus invoked, one should worship the Durgā-yantra with water for the feet (pādya) and other offerings. Reciting the root mantra: "I offer water for the feet to Śrī Durgā; obeisance. In the same manner, [one offers] the arghya, the water for sipping (ācamanīya), and the honey-mixture (madhuparka).

"I offer pure water, unguents for anointing, bathing water, and again water for sipping. Having thus bathed [the deity] and visualized the wiping of the limbs, at the end of the root mantra: "I offer a garment to Durgā;
obeisance! [I offer] fragrance, unbroken rice grains, vermilion, and flowers. Then, with the root mantra...
Having offered five handfuls of flowers: *hrāṃ hrīṃ duṃ durgāyai hṛdayāya namaḥ*; *hrīṃ hrīṃ duṃ durgāyai śirase svāhā*; *hrūṃ hrīṃ duṃ durgāyai śikhāyai vaṣaṭ*.

Hraiṃ Hrīṃ Duṃ, obeisance to Durgā’s armor, Huṃ! Hrauṃ Hrīṃ Duṃ, obeisance to Durgā’s three eyes, Vauṣaṭ! Hraṃḥ Hrīṃ Duṃ, obeisance to Durgā’s weapon, Phaṭ! In this manner, one should perform the worship.
Then, upon the petals starting from the east: Jaṃ, obeisance to Jayā; Viṃ, obeisance to Vijayā; Kiṃ, obeisance to Kīrti.

Namaḥ! Prīṃ, obeisance to Prīti (Affection)! Praṃ, obeisance to Pramā (Faithful Resolve)! Śaṃ, obeisance to Śraddhā (Faith)! Maṃ, obeisance to Medhā (Intelligence)! Śaṃ, obeisance to Śruti (Sacred Revelation)! (p. 20b)

On the tips of the petals, starting from the east: *śaṃ* salutation to Śaṅkha; *caṃ* salutation to Cakra; *gaṃ* salutation to Gadā; *khaṃ* salutation to Khaḍga; *paṃ* salutation to Pāśa; *aṃ* salutation to Aṅkuśa; *śaṃ* salutation to Śara; *caṃ* salutation to Cāpa. Outside of that: *indrāya namaḥ*.
Salutation to Agni. Salutation to Yama. Salutation to Nirṛti. Salutation to Varuṇa. Salutation to Vāyu.
Salutation to Kubera. Salutation to Īśāna. Between the East and Īśāna, salutation to Brahmā. Between Nirṛti and Varuṇa...
Homage to Ananta. In this very same sequence: homage to Vajra; homage to Śakti; homage to Daṇḍa;
homage to Khaḍga; homage to Pāśa; homage to Aṅkuśa; homage to Gadā.

"Salutation to the trident; salutation to the lotus; salutation to the discus," and so on, having thus worshipped, one should offer the worship of all the surrounding enclosures with devotion, saying:
"O You who are compassionate toward those who have come for refuge, grant me the attainment of my desired goal;
I offer this entire worship of the enclosures unto You."
Having thus prepared the water for washing the feet (*arghyodaka*) at the feet of the Deity, one should offer incense. Having consecrated the incense vessel with *phaṭ*, one should say *namaḥ*.

Having thus worshipped, at the end of the root mantra: "Obeisance, I offer incense to the venerable Durgā, together with her limbs and her retinue. One should offer it with water from the *argha* vessel. "Jagaddhvani mantramātassvāhā.
Having thus worshipped the bell, ringing it with the left hand, [one should worship] from the feet upwards of the Deity.

One should offer incense up to the navel. Following this same sequence, one should place the lamp from the feet up to the eyes; the incense vessel should be placed on the left side of the deity and the lamp vessel on the right.

Then, having brought as an offering (naivedya) whatever is available— such as milk-rice (pāyasa), ghee, and water— and having given the water for sipping (ācamanīya) to the deity with the root mantra, [he should recite] "phaṭ."

Having sprinkled [the offering] and recited the root mantra eight times, having rendered it nectarine with the *dhenumudrā* while uttering "vaṃ," and having worshipped it with "namaḥ," while touching the vessel with the left thumb and visualizing that light has issued from the mouth of the Deity,
[one offers] this food-offering (*naivedya*) to Śrī Durgā, together with her limbs and her retinue.

"I offer this; salutations! Having thus offered the water for the *argha*, one should display the five mudrās, beginning with *prāṇa*, using the right hand. Then, having given the water for sipping (*ācamanīya*) with the root mantra— (p.

Having put on the upper garment and recited the root mantra as much as possible, one should remove the upper garment, perform the previously mentioned nyāsas of the seers (ṛṣis) and so forth, and having sipped water (ācamana), offer a portion of the food offering (naivedya) in the northeast direction with the words: "Obeisance to Śeṣikā, the consumer of the remains of the offerings. Then, with the root mantra, offer betel leaves (tāmbūla) as a gift.
One should display the parasol, the fly-whisk, and the mirror. Having performed the *ārārtika* rite with the root mantra:
"The intellect, together with its latent impressions (*vāsanā*), is fashioned as the mirror and the auspicious objects;
your manifold mental fluctuations are conceived in the form of the dance."
Sound, by way of its division into vocal and instrumental forms, [is of two kinds].
O Lord, these lotuses have been fashioned by me as umbrellas for you.
The Suṣumṇā exists in the form of a banner, and the vital breaths (prāṇas) and others exist in the form of chowries.
The ego-sense is fashioned as an elephant, and its momentum is conceived as a chariot.
The senses, in the form of horses, [carry] sounds and other objects along the path of the chariot.
This discernment, acting as the reins for the mind, is the charioteer.
Everything else has been likewise fashioned as an instrument for you.
Having thus recited the mantras for the offering of oneself.

O Goddess, may my senses always be the flowers; may the guru be the incense, this body the lamp, and my life-breath, ego, vigor, and compassion be the nine unbroken grains (akṣata). May he now partake of the fruit of this worship.
The individual soul.
Anointed with saffron and smeared with sandalwood paste.
Having fashioned a funeral cake with bilva leaves, he has come to my home, O Durgā, seeking refuge.
Grant me beauty, grant me victory, O Blessed One, grant me fortune!
Grant me sons, grant me wealth, and grant me all my desires.
O slayer of Mahisha, O great illusionist, O Chamunda, O wearer of a garland of severed heads!
O Goddess, grant me long life, health, and sovereignty; salutations to you!
Having thus offered a handful of flowers (*puṣpāñjali*) and taken water in his cupped palms, [he says]: "From this point forward, by virtue of my life-force, intellect, body, and religious duties..."
"Whatever has been remembered, spoken, or done by me through mind, speech, or action— with my two hands, my feet, my belly, and my genitals— during the states of waking, dreaming, and deep sleep,
may all that be offered to the deity Śrī Durgā. Having thus offered this, having performed circumambulation, and having prostrated;

Having taken the *argha* water, having whirled it three times and held it with the face turned away, one should worship the *argha* vessel, saying: "Obeisance to the *argha* vessel of Śrī Durgā and the others. (p.
Having formed the *saṃhāramudrā*:
"Go, go to the supreme place, your own abode, O Supreme Goddess!"
Wherein the gods, beginning with Brahmā, do not know the supreme state.

Having recited this, one should take the flower from the yantra and apply it to the nostrils; one should then visualize that the form of radiant energy (tejas) drawn in by the flower has entered the heart via the path of the nose. Having said, "By this worship, may the venerable Goddess Durgā be pleased," one should apply a tilaka with the root mantra, drink the water from her feet, and [partake of] the food offering (naivedya).
Having herself partaken of a small portion, Śrī Durgā should contemplate her own self as divided; such is the concise procedure for the daily worship.
May it be auspicious!
